page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv6 family, powered by a 3.4 GHz ARM-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. The server features 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 1890 GB local disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is a key strength; both large-block read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks rank in the top 10%, supported by a top-tier Passmark memory score. Database operations also perform exceptionally well, scoring in the top 10% on Passmark database tests, while Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput register in the top 25%.

While multi-threaded tasks like software compilation and bzip3 decompression show strong results, single-core performance remains average. Additionally, the server exhibits a clear performance tradeoff in large-scale machine learning tasks, with LLM inference prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the bottom 10%. Consequently, this instance is highly cost-efficient for resource-dense workloads such as database management, web serving, and multi-threaded application hosting, but is less suitable for heavy single-threaded execution or large-scale AI model inference.
